rationale: Round 1 compiled, ran correctly, and hit no ICE fallback, so this candidate shifts the table toward stronger obfuscation on this small (4.3KB text, 19-function) C++ symbolic-differentiation benchmark. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain since flattening the large quotient_expr::deriv (1917B) and prod_expr::deriv bodies gives the biggest analysis resistance, with moderate cost weights to keep the interpreter-style dispatch overhead tolerable in the derivative-evaluation hot path. BCF is pushed up (SecurityGain 0.8) to add opaque-predicate layering on top of flattening, accepting modest size growth since the binary is tiny and headroom is ample. SUB and SPLIT stay near-zero-cost workhorses with high DiversityGain to maximize per-function structural divergence across the many small methods. IBR and ICALL are raised moderately to obscure the class-method call graph characteristic of this C++ source, with CorrectnessRisk kept below 0.35 to protect the vtable-dependent dispatch. IGV remains the weakest signal: it adds little on a program with few globals and carries the highest correctness risk against C++ static initialization, so it is effectively a low-priority filler. Overall the table trades the safety margin proven in round 1 for a notably higher obfuscation density while capping runtime-weighted costs so the benchmark's execution time stays acceptable.
